heading: Polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure, so alone it is not evidence of superposition
definition: polysemantic neurons can arise for other reasons, so they aren't by themselves evidence of superposition.
summary: Several groups independent of the original study find mixed-selective neurons, which respond to several features, in toy networks with more than enough units; the routes differ, such as the range of values the underlying source variables take, or nonlinear feature contamination, where neurons pick up extra features. One study of real transformers finds word-level (lexical) confounds in polysemanticity measurements, but it does not show polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 for toy networks (size not stated by the script), for the existential claim only. This rests on studies from groups other than the original's. arXiv:2211.09169 shares an author with the original, so it counts as same-group (R1-type) evidence. R0 for lexical-confound evidence at <1B and 10-100B (arXiv:2604.00443). Its Pythia-1B validation also gives R0 evidence at 1-10B, although counts has no 1-10B bucket. Real-model results do not establish absent capacity pressure. >100B untested.
suggested_status.reason: Toy-network studies from groups other than the original's report mixing despite sufficient dimensions, through different mechanisms: source-support effects (arXiv:2410.06232#r3) and nonlinear feature contamination with m ≥ Θ(d0) (arXiv:2406.03345#R1). arXiv:2211.09169 reports equal-loss solutions with different polysemanticity (arXiv:2211.09169#arXiv2211.09169-R1). It shares an author, Nicholas Schiefer, with Toy Models of Superposition (author list and reference EHO+22b, per the checker). It is the study behind counts: versions.V3.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1, and it counts as same-group (R1-type) evidence, not as independent. Its spare capacity is in the nonlinear layer (k=1024 > N=512); the compressed input stays at d=64. So R2 rests on the other groups. It covers the existential claim reached through different mechanisms, not a reproduction of any one mechanism. arXiv:2410.06232's omitted-source result (r16) is not part of this basis: the neurons stay modular and only appear mixed-selective when a correlated source is left out of the analysis. That is a measurement caution, not an origin of polysemanticity. counts: versions.V3.studies_with_challenges = 0 and counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies = 10 were made from the verdict records before the checks, and counts.json has not been rebuilt since. No V3 check-log entry moves a verdict to challenges. The checks set these V3 verdicts to none: lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv's only V3 verdict (supports); arXiv:2410.06232's omitted-source supports verdict; and arXiv:2610.20851's limits_scope verdict. So counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.studies = 10 still counts lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv, and counts: versions.V3.verdicts.supports.verdicts = 12 includes both lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv's verdict and arXiv:2410.06232's omitted-source verdict. The checks confirm the other supports verdicts of arXiv:2410.06232 (source support) and arXiv:2610.20851 (exact capacity). These studies keep at least one V3 supports verdict that no check-log entry sets to none: arXiv:2211.09169 (same group), arXiv:2312.03096, arXiv:2406.03345, arXiv:2410.06232 (source-support verdict only), arXiv:2504.08842, arXiv:2604.00443, arXiv:2610.20851, lw:8EyCQKuWo6swZpagS and lw:sEyWufriufTnBKnTG. None of the verdicts set to none is part of the R2 basis above. The transformer evidence (arXiv:2604.00443#r1, #r3, #r15) shows lexical confounding of the measurements, not origins free of capacity pressure. Scale coverage follows versions.V3.studies_by_size, except that the Pythia-1B result in arXiv:2604.00443#r15 has no 1-10B entry there.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would raise a mechanism above R0: a second, independent group reproducing one specific mechanism (incidental collisions, feature contamination, or source-support mixing). That would put the mechanism itself at R2, not only the existential claim. Would strengthen the real-model status: an independent replication of the lexical controls. Would extend the causal claim: capacity-controlled training of real models that separates the alternative mechanisms from superposition. Population-level measurements would show how common these mechanisms are. Would move the level toward C: a failed reproduction of the toy mechanisms by another group.

source.title: Toy Models of Superposition
source.authors: Nelson Elhage; Tristan Hume; Catherine Olsson; Nicholas Schiefer; T. Henighan; S. Kravec; Zac Hatfield-Dodds; R. Lasenby; Dawn Drain; Carol Chen; R. Grosse; Sam McCandlish; J. Kaplan; D. Amodei; M. Wattenberg; Chris Olah

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Toy decoder tasks had polysemantic minima matching monosemantic ones in loss; bias initialization could avoid them.
Toy autoencoders developed polysemantic neurons despite enough neurons for monosemantic solutions.
Neurons mixing several source variables arose with spare capacity, driven by dependence between the variables' ranges.
Two-layer ReLU networks mixed label-uncorrelated features into neurons even with spare capacity.
Even with 16 hidden neurons to compute 8 pairwise ANDs, networks used overlapping polysemantic codes.
In nine transformers, neurons overlapped more for the same word in different senses than for synonyms.
Toy autoencoder neurons became polysemantic despite room for a monosemantic solution.
Small toy MLPs found polysemantic solutions with fewer features than neurons.
Procgen Heist CNN channels responded to all entities at different magnitudes; SAEs did not split them.
Toy classifiers with exactly enough neurons stayed polysemantic given spherical data or weight-decay-free linear outputs.
Neurons in two-layer linear networks did not accumulate label-uncorrelated features, so this mixing needs nonlinearity.
With weight decay or sparse non-negative latents, models with exactly enough neurons moved toward monosemantic neurons.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Directly establishing non-capacity origins, and their prevalence, in pretrained real models through controlled changes in capacity.
untested.basis: arXiv:2604.00443 tests lexical confounding without showing absent capacity pressure. lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv (reduced IMPALA CNN, Procgen Heist, checkpoint 35001) reports multi-entity magnitude coding in conv3a/conv4a: mean entity-trajectory correlation 0.956 in conv3a and 0.931 in conv4a (lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv#r1, lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv#r2, lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv#r3). Individual conv4a latents of a 4x SAE keep this coding (lw:XWmqSTX89rgqeqyfv#r6). The study has no capacity manipulation or higher-capacity comparison, and SAE non-separation cannot tell superposition apart from a non-capacity origin, so it does not test this part. The checks set its only V3 label to none and these rows to cannot_determine for V3. arXiv:2610.20851's pretrained-model analyses (Sections 5.4 and 9.4) measure associations between neuron interpretability and cross-model matching, with no controlled capacity intervention. The paper does not itself say this is untested; the gap follows from its design. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training.by_family contains only 'other or not stated'. The named families (GPT-2, Llama, Pythia) appear only under the measurement, probing and removal keys of versions.V3.coverage_by_operation, not under training.

untested.what: Tests above 100B and controlled comparisons of these mechanisms across base, instruction-tuned, and preference-trained stages.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V3.studies_by_size has no >100B entry; versions.V3.studies_by_stage has other, not stated, and reasoning, but no base, instruct/chat, or preference/RL entries. untested.what: Whether the incidental-collision mechanism and its neuron-count scaling persist when features co-occur in the tied-weight autoencoder.
untested.basis: lw:sEyWufriufTnBKnTG explicitly lists feature co-occurrence as untested; arXiv:2312.03096 uses basis-vector data. counts: versions.V3.coverage_by_operation.training records training coverage but does not establish this mechanism-specific distributional extension.

wording_issues.phrase: aren't by themselves evidence of superposition
wording_issues.issue: The evidence supports treating polysemanticity as not enough to identify superposition uniquely. It does not establish that polysemanticity has no evidential value, or that superposition is absent wherever an alternative mechanism is found. The source-support study shows mixing in networks with more units than sources under source-support manipulations, but does not directly establish that superposition is absent. In a reduced IMPALA CNN on Procgen Heist (checkpoint 35001), shared channels respond to different entities with different activation magnitudes. Mean entity-trajectory correlations are 0.956 in conv3a and 0.931 in conv4a (matched trajectories in a simplified T-shaped maze). In fork-maze patching, individual latents of a 4x conv4a SAE still steer by magnitude toward more than one entity. Most of the successful interventions exceed the 99.9th percentile of normal activations. The fact that the SAE does not separate the entities establishes neither absent capacity pressure nor absent superposition. The check set this study's V3 verdict to none and its rows r1–r3 and r6 to cannot_determine for V3.

The studies measure this as mixed selectivity, feature-weight projections, overlapping Boolean codes, or lexical overlap. Whether these measures are equivalent is not established. Feature contamination is measured as simultaneous core/background feature-weight projections (Theorem 4.2), and Appendix G.3 contrasts it with capacity-limited superposition. Whether it corresponds to interpretability definitions of polysemanticity is neither tested nor explicitly discussed. The multiplication example is qualitative and depends on which features are taken as natural.

The alternative reasons have different scopes. They are: initialization collisions under ℓ1 regularization in tied-weight toy autoencoders (an analytic estimate for m ≥ n, plus a width sweep); nonlinear feature contamination; source-support constraints; and lexical confounding of measurements. The lexical study gives a measurement alternative without showing an origin free of capacity pressure. The source-support study also reports a measurement effect: leaving a correlated, encoded source out of the analysis makes neurons that stay modular appear mixed-selective (linear RNN, three-object task). The check set this result's V3 verdict to none: it is a measurement caution, not an origin of polysemantic neurons.

method_sensitivity.what: Zero-bias feature decoders reach equal-loss solutions with different polysemanticity; negative bias promotes monosemanticity. Negative bias does not eliminate polysemantic basins in the absolute-value task.

An analytic estimate from random-initialization benign collisions predicts about n(n−1)/(4m), approximately n²/(4m), polysemantic neurons for the ℓ1-regularized tied-weight autoencoder with m ≥ n (arXiv:2312.03096#r1). This is a theoretical derivation, not a measurement on a trained model, and it is not limited to the width sweep. In trained width sweeps (n=256, m=256–4096; 16 runs in r2), the reported polysemantic-neuron trend is Θ(n²/m). The informal report states the same trend over the same sweep (lw:sEyWufriufTnBKnTG#r1). Without ℓ1, a single bipolar-noise instance (σ=0.01, size not stated) gives an encoding that shares 7 neurons with other features (r3). It does not establish the same scaling under noise.

method_sensitivity.factor: Source-support geometry, frequency relations, and variables included in the analysis
method_sensitivity.what: These are nonnegative, energy-regularized networks with more units than sources. Removing source-support corners degrades modularity (r3, r5). In the What-Where feedforward network, the two conditions in r4 differ. Range-preserving correlations add some mixing, but less than matched corner cutting. Removing diagonal data adds no mixing. In the autoencoder, range-preserving correlations or removing central data cause less mixing than corner cutting (r6). In linear RNNs, harmonic frequencies mix, while irrational or rational non-harmonic frequencies modularize (r8, r9). Analysis setting: in a linear RNN on a three-object task, leaving a correlated encoded object out of the neuron analysis makes neurons that stay modular look mixed-selective (r16). This is a measurement caution, not a different origin of actual polysemantic neurons.
ReLU networks accumulate background features, whereas matched identity-activation networks do not. This limits the contamination mechanism to the tested nonlinear conditions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Latent distribution, output activation, regularization, and training budget
method_sensitivity.what: At exact capacity (m=n′=5), hyperspherical latents keep mixed selectivity with linear or ReLU output (r3, r4). Sparse nonnegative latents keep mixing with unregularized linear output (r2). With sparse nonnegative latents and ReLU output, axis alignment develops slowly and varies by seed. Without weight decay, 3/10 runs reach MCC ≥ 0.90 within 1,000,000 updates; median final MCC is 0.878 (IQR 0.816–0.895) (Section 9.1, per the checker). So r1's convergence to axis alignment holds only partly within this budget. With energy regularization (weight decay 0.03), linear output reaches MCC 0.968. That value comes from a separate regularized ablation and is given in the verdict reason, not a row; the r2–r4 comparisons use zero weight decay. These results show how much alignment each setting gives. They are not evidence against V3's claim that polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.

method_sensitivity.factor: Lexical controls, layer, and subspace removal
method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2, the lexical contribution ratio Rlex falls from 0.74 to 0.29 across layers (r2). Projecting out k=20 lexical components (0.7% of dimensions) changes the PS–SYN cosine gap from 0.119 to 0.047 and Rlex from 0.65 to 0.41 (r11). At k=50 the gap becomes −0.028 (r12). The 37–51% cross-model reduction in Table 10 is a reduction in Rlex, not in the gap. The row's note gives it as a gap reduction. The gap reversal shows sensitivity to lexical identity; it is not a reversal of V3.
